assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Torrent Pharmaceuticals (consolidated, ₹ crore), on the basis that holds over the target horizon: Torrent with 100% of J.B. Chemicals & Pharmaceuticals (JB) merged in (scheme effective 8-Jul-2026, appointed date 21-Jan-2026) and 38.04 cr shares (4.19 cr allotted on 20-Jul-2026). The base year FY26 is a pro forma combined year (TORNTPHARM.patch.js: revenue ₹17,352 cr per AR FY26 note 42; acquisition interest for the full year), so FY27E growth is like-for-like. One reportable segment (generic formulations), so the engine runs on a single revenue-growth path; the business-line build (India base, JB India, Brazil, US, Germany, rest of world, JB international & CDMO) sits in `businessLines` and the authoring script checks it sums to model revenue. Depreciation includes ₹1,340 cr a year of amortisation of JB's brands and customer relationships created in the purchase accounting (not tax-deductible; a deferred-tax credit offsets it in book tax). No minorities from FY27. Valued on EV/EBITDA on Sep-28E EBITDA, as Prabhudas Lilladher and ICICI Direct do (unaffected by the JB amortisation and the new debt); P/E on EPS before the JB amortisation (Motilal Oswal's method) and a DCF are cross-checks.
assumptions._revenueWhy: Sum of the business-line build below, on the pro forma FY26 base of ₹17,352 cr (reported FY26 ₹13,980 cr had JB for 70 days). FY27E ₹19,513 cr = +40% on reported FY26, +12.5% like-for-like: India base +16% (Q1 +19%, management 'mid-teens', semaglutide injectable out of stock Jul-Aug), JB India +10% (Q1 +13%; brand transfers to Torrent divisions disrupt Q2-Q3; management 'double-digit still possible'), Brazil +16% in rupees (Q1 +3% in BRL after a one-off channel destocking; mid-teens from Q2), US +12% in rupees (Q1 +23% in dollars incl. one-offs; single-digit dollar growth guided), Germany +4% (supplier out of business, lost tenders), rest of world +8%, JB international and CDMO +10% ('high single to low double digit'). FY28-29E: India base +14%/+13%, JB India +11% (revenue synergies only from FY28), Brazil +13%/+12%, US +6%/+5%, Germany +4%, rest of world +8%, JB international +10%.

businessLines._why: FY26 pro forma by line: Torrent's FY26 split (AR FY26 MD&A: India ₹7,645 cr, US ₹1,363 cr, Germany ₹1,249 cr, Brazil ₹1,362 cr, others ₹2,361 cr) less JB's 70-day contribution (₹775 cr: India ₹438 cr = Q4 India ₹2,215 cr less Torrent base India ₹1,777 cr [Q4FY25 ₹1,545 cr +15%], international ₹337 cr), plus JB's full FY26 revenue (₹4,148 cr, Screener JBCHEPHARM) split 61/39 India/international as in Q1FY27 (₹733 cr / ₹468 cr of ₹1,201 cr). Growth rates are explained in _revenueWhy.

assumptions._marginWhy: Q1FY27 33.8% (Torrent base 33.3%, JB 35.3% vs 28.8% a year earlier). Built from the two businesses: Torrent base margin +50bp a year (management's standing guidance: 32.8% FY26 → 33.3% / 33.8% / 34.3%); JB 35.5% / 37.5% / 38.5% as the ₹400-450 cr cost synergies (guided for year 3, 'tracking ahead', FY27 'definitely above ₹100 cr') are delivered, against 26.7% in JB's own FY26 books. Weighted: 33.8% / 34.7% / 35.3%. Each 1pp of margin is ~₹217 cr of FY28E EBITDA (~₹4.2 of EPS).
assumptions._capexWhy: FY26 ₹677 cr (incl. JB for 70 days), FY25 ₹612 cr; JB's own capex ~₹110-200 cr a year (cash flow FY24-26). Combined ~₹800 cr in FY27E rising with revenue (~4% of sales). No acquisitions assumed: management will wait 12-18 months before the next deal.
assumptions._depWhy: Q1FY27 D&A ₹593 cr (₹2,372 cr annualised): Torrent ~₹205 cr a quarter, JB's own ~₹45 cr, ~₹335 cr of amortisation of JB brands and customer relationships (₹1,340 cr a year: the Q4FY26 stub was ₹257 cr for 70 days and the CFO said to use it for the full year; brands ₹19,627 cr amortised over up to 15 years). 5.83% of the average gross block (₹40,426 cr at Mar-26 incl. ₹20,691 cr of JB intangibles) gives ₹2,380 / 2,428 / 2,479 cr. CWIP is held flat by the engine.
assumptions._treasuryWhy: Set to zero because the engine applies the yield to net cash, which is negative (net debt ₹12,684 cr at Mar-26). Treasury income on the gross cash and fund balance is built in otherIncome instead.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Built from sourced parts (AR FY26 note 29). (1) Treasury income: interest ₹38.4 cr + mutual-fund gains ₹30.9 cr = ₹69.4 cr in FY26, when JB's ₹1,155 cr of cash and funds came in only in January; gross cash, bank and funds ₹2,031 cr at Mar-26, assumed ₹1,500 cr from Mar-27 as surplus cash repays commercial paper; 6.25% gives ₹110 cr in FY27E and ₹94 cr a year after. (2) Foreign exchange and hedging: +₹170 cr FY22, -₹18 cr FY23, -₹4 cr FY24, -₹17 cr FY25, -₹183 cr FY26 (forward-cover losses as the rupee fell; ~₹45 cr in Q3FY26 alone), still negative in Q1FY27 (PL: other income -₹12 cr 'led by forex loss'): we take -₹100 cr in FY27E, -₹40 cr in FY28E and -₹20 cr in FY29E as the old hedges run off (FY23-25 average -₹13 cr). (3) Recurring miscellaneous non-operating income ₹3 cr (FY26 ₹2.8 cr). Left out as one-offs: asset-sale gains (₹17.7 cr in FY26) and exceptional items (FY26 -₹89 cr: ₹70 cr deal costs and ₹19 cr JB distribution severance; Q1FY27 -₹21 cr). Total ₹13 / 57 / 77 cr vs FY26 -₹94 cr (reported other income) and -₹69 cr in the twelve months to Jun-26 (Screener, before exceptional items).
assumptions._interestLabel: Interest on borrowings (₹10,990 cr acquisition NCDs at 7.45-7.80%) and leases
assumptions._interestWhy: Q1FY27 finance cost ₹305 cr on ₹14,798 cr of borrowings (Mar-26: NCDs ₹11,161 cr, commercial paper ₹1,420 cr, working-capital loans ₹1,495 cr, term loans ₹723 cr) plus ₹227 cr of leases. Acquisition debt raised in Jan-2026: ₹1,500 cr one-year CP and NCDs of ₹2,000 / 2,500 / 3,000 / 3,500 cr maturing in 2, 3, 4 and 5 years at 7.45% / 7.60% / 7.70% / 7.80% (weighted 7.66%). Built as 7.7% on average gross borrowings (our net-debt path in the authoring script plus ₹1,500-2,031 cr of gross cash) plus ~₹55 cr of lease and other finance costs: borrowings fall from ₹14,798 cr to ~₹12,700 / 9,900 / 6,700 cr at Mar-27/28/29 as free cash flow repays CP and working-capital lines, then the ₹2,100 cr and ₹2,590 cr NCD maturities (FY28, FY29).
assumptions._taxWhy: Book tax on profit after the JB brand amortisation: FY26 25.6% (₹734 cr on ₹2,872 cr), Q1FY27 22.8% (current tax ₹254 cr, deferred-tax credit ₹87 cr on ₹733 cr). The brand amortisation is not tax-deductible, but the deferred tax liability created in the purchase accounting unwinds at 25.17% of it, so the book rate stays near the statutory 25.17%. No minorities after the merger (JB's subsidiaries are wholly owned).
assumptions._payoutWhy: Torrent paid out 57-59% of profit in FY24-26 (FY26: ₹29 interim + ₹9 final = ₹38 a share on 33.84 cr shares). We assume 50% while net debt is above ~1x EBITDA (management targets deleveraging over 2-3 years); DPS ~₹31 / ₹41 / ₹52.

dcf._betaWhy: The engine discounts at the cost of equity; beta 0.78 gives 11.2%, equal to our WACC: market value ~₹1.83 lakh cr, net debt ₹12,684 cr (6.5% of capital) at 7.7% pre-tax (5.8% after tax), cost of equity ~11.6% at beta 0.85 for a defensive, domestically led pharma company.
dcf._tgWhy: 6% nominal: India branded generics (~55% of revenue) grow 8-10% a year in value; Germany and the US grow little.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from ~11% to 8% by year 15 as the India franchise matures and export markets stay low-growth.
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: 35%: a little below the FY29E 35.3% (base margin +50bp a year cannot continue forever; price controls, trade generics).
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: 4.5% of revenue: maintenance plus capacity for 8% growth (FY24-27E 3.5-4.8%).
dcf._depWhy: 5% of revenue = tax-deductible depreciation and amortisation only (book D&A ex-JB brand amortisation ~5.3% of FY27E revenue). The JB brand amortisation is excluded because it gives no tax saving; including it would overstate cash flow.

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: India keeps growing mid-teens (semaglutide recovers, Curatio +30%), the JB brand transfer is smooth and revenue synergies start in FY28, Brazil approves generic semaglutide, and cost synergies reach ₹450 cr a year early.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: The JB integration loses prescribers (as some past brand transfers did), India growth slips back to ~10% as the market normalises, Germany keeps losing tenders, semaglutide prices collapse, and synergies are reinvested rather than banked.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.why: How the street values Torrent: two of the three post-Q1 notes that disclose a method use EV/EBITDA on FY28E (Prabhudas Lilladher 28x, ICICI Direct 27x; Motilal Oswal uses P/E). EV/EBITDA is also unaffected by the two things the JB deal changed: ~₹1,340 cr a year of non-cash brand amortisation and the new debt. 21x = Torrent's 19.9x median one-year-forward EV/EBITDA since Apr-2021 (computed in our files: before the deal on Torrent's own 33.84 cr shares, net debt and standalone EBITDA; after the 29-Jun-2025 announcement on 38.04 cr shares, the deal debt and combined forward EBITDA; no trough years) x 1.0555 (pharma peers' median trailing EV/EBITDA vs five-year medians at 30-Sep-2026, excluding Torrent: the EV/EBITDA analogue of the PLAYBOOK §7c P/E factor, as for hospitals) = 21.0x. Bull 26x and bear 18x = the 75th (24.8x) and 25th (17.1x) percentiles x 1.0555. Sep-28E EBITDA less net debt at Sep-28E (model).

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: Cross-check on earnings (Motilal Oswal's method). 42x Sep-28E EPS BEFORE the JB brand amortisation (₹1,340 cr a year, ~₹26 a share after its deferred-tax credit), because the P/E history is pre-deal Torrent that never carried it: Torrent's 40.0x median one-year-forward P/E since Apr-2021 on EPS before exceptional items (batch rule, as Sun Pharma and Cipla) x 1.0545 (PLAYBOOK §7c pharma P/E factor) = 42.2x → 42x. The engine values reported EPS, so the multiple here is the equivalent on reported Sep-28E EPS (42 x adjusted ÷ reported: base 53.66x; bull 46.5x and bear 36x on the adjusted basis, translated the same way). Checked in TORNTPHARM.ctx.js.

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: Tests whether cash flows support the price: 15-year FCFF at 11.2% (beta set so the cost of equity equals our WACC), terminal growth 6%; tax shield only on tax-deductible depreciation (JB brand amortisation excluded); less net debt at Mar-27.

otherTreasury.label: Offset: minority interest (₹9,196 cr, now equity) and deferred tax on JB brands (₹5,670 cr) in other liabilities
otherTreasury._why: Engine workaround (TORNTPHARM.patch.js note 2). Screener's Mar-26 other liabilities, which the Excel model reads unpatched, include the ₹9,196.40 cr non-controlling interest (now owners' equity after the merger) and the ₹5,670.04 cr deferred tax liability; neither is working capital. This negative entry takes both out of working capital (13.45% of pro forma revenue) in the engine and the Excel alike; investments are raised by the same amount in the patch, so net debt is unchanged at ₹12,913 cr incl. leases, and CWIP is lowered by the DTL so the balance sheet balances.

cover.headline: India's best brand-builder has bought JB with debt: a franchise worth owning, but at ₹4,800 the price runs well ahead of Torrent's own valuation history
cover.lead: Torrent is India's 5th-largest pharma company after merging J.B. Chemicals (effective 8-Jul-2026; 38.04 cr shares), #1 in cardiac, with 75% of India sales in chronic therapies, plus branded generics in Brazil and generics in the US and Germany. Q1FY27 revenue rose 55% to ₹4,921 cr (base business +17%, India +19%; JB +10% with its margin up from 28.8% to 35.3%). The price of the deal is a reset: ₹12,500 cr of debt (net debt 2.3x EBITDA) and ₹1,340 cr a year of non-cash brand amortisation, so FY26 pro forma EPS is ₹35.0. We forecast EBITDA of ₹6,596 / 7,527 / 8,473 cr and EPS of ₹{{F.eps.0|n1}} / {{F.eps.1|n1}} / {{F.eps.2|n1}} for FY27-29E (₹88.1 / 109.8 / 131.8 before the JB amortisation). Two of the three brokers that disclose a method value Torrent on **EV/EBITDA on FY28E** (PL 28x, ICICI Direct 27x; Motilal Oswal uses P/E), and so do we: **21x Sep-28E EBITDA of ₹8,000 cr** (Torrent's own 19.9x forward median since 2021, lifted 5.55% for the sector's EV/EBITDA re-rating), less net debt, gives **{{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): we initiate with SELL.** Cross-checks: P/E 42x Sep-28E EPS before the JB amortisation (₹120.8) gives ₹5,075; DCF ₹3,362. Bull {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

arguments.h: A domestic compounder with a proven acquisition playbook
arguments.p: Base business +15% in FY26 (India +13%) and India +19% in Q1FY27 against the market's 9-12%, 27 brands above ₹100 cr, a 7,000-rep field force with high productivity. Elder (2014), Unichem (2017) and Curatio (2022, +27-34% a year since) all grew faster under Torrent; JB's brands (Cilacar, Nicardia, Metrogyl, Rantac) make it #1 in cardiac.

arguments.h: JB is working so far, earlier than planned
arguments.p: JB's margin jumped to 35.3% in its first full quarter (26.7% in its own FY26 books), field-force attrition fell from ~30% to 16%, and FY27 cost synergies will be "definitely above ₹100 cr" against ₹90 cr planned (₹400-450 cr by year 3). The risk is the brand transfers into Torrent divisions in Q2-Q3, which management says can dent revenue for 2-3 quarters.

arguments.h: The generics half is not a moat
arguments.p: US sales are about where they were in FY14 in dollars; Germany is "in the middle of the woods" after a supplier failure and lost tenders; Brazil grows but lost the first-mover slot in semaglutide. sections.title: A branded-generics company: India and Brazil brands carry the profits, US and German generics add scale

blocks.p: Torrent sells prescription medicines under its own brand names to doctors (branded generics) and plain generic copies to insurers, pharmacies and wholesalers. **India** is the core: ₹7,645 cr in FY26, 55% of revenue, 75% of it in chronic and sub-chronic therapies (cardiac 31%, gastro 21%, CNS 12%), sold through ~7,000 medical representatives (9,300 with JB). Curatio, bought in 2022, adds cosmetic dermatology and consumer brands growing ~30% a year. **Brazil** (₹1,362 cr, BRL 817 mn) is a second branded market where Torrent is the largest Indian company. **The US** (₹1,363 cr, US$151 mn) and **Germany** (₹1,249 cr, EUR 121 mn) are generics businesses: price takers in tenders and wholesaler contracts. **Rest of world** (₹2,361 cr) includes the Philippines, Russia, Mexico, Sri Lanka and, from 21-Jan-2026, JB's export and contract-manufacturing (CDMO) business.

**J.B. Chemicals (JB)**, now merged, adds ₹4,148 cr of FY26 revenue (JB's own books; EBITDA ₹1,107 cr, 26.7%): about 61% India (Cilacar and Nicardia in hypertension, Metrogyl, Rantac, Sporlac; an in-licensed Novartis ophthalmology range; Azmarda in heart failure) and 39% international and CDMO (lozenges for multinational customers; Russia, South Africa, the US). JB's IQVIA sales were ₹2,749 cr in FY25, of which cardiac ₹1,214 cr. Together the two are #5 in the Indian market, #4 in chronic therapies and #1 in cardiac.

sections.title: India is a branded, doctor-driven market growing ~10%; Torrent has grown faster for three years

blocks.p: The Indian pharmaceutical market (IPM) is worth over US$27 bn and grew ~8% in FY26 (AR FY26); growth picked up to ~12% in the Jun-2026 quarter (AIOCD Pharmatrac: volume 2.0%, price 5.8%, new products 3.3%). Chronic therapies (cardiac, diabetes, CNS, gastro) are ~56% of the IPM and grow faster than acute; they are 75% of Torrent's India sales. In India doctors choose the brand, so companies compete through field forces, brand recall and steady supply rather than price. Scale matters: bigger companies can afford more reps per doctor and can relaunch acquired brands through them, which is why the market keeps consolidating. Outside India the picture is different: US and German generics are commodity markets with steady price erosion, where only cost, supply reliability and new launches matter.

blocks.p: **Brazil** (₹1,362 cr in FY26; BRL 817 mn, +12% in local currency) is a branded-generics market like India: Torrent is the largest Indian company, 19th in retail, with 33 branded and 27 generic products and 58 awaiting ANVISA approval. blocks.callout: **Honest verdict:** Torrent has a genuine moat in India: doctors' prescription habits for its chronic brands are sticky, its scale lets it out-promote smaller owners of the same brands, and four acquisitions show it can buy brands and grow them faster. That moat covers ~55% of revenue (56% with JB). Brazil is a smaller version of the same model. The US and Germany have no moat at all: they are cost-and-supply businesses that have not grown in a decade in local currency. The JB deal deepens the moat (#1 in cardiac) but was paid for with debt and a full price, so returns on capital stay below FY25 levels until FY29E.

sections.title: Revenue +64% and margins +4pp since FY22; the JB deal lifts revenue by a third but halves EPS for now

blocks.p: Torrent's revenue grew from ₹8,508 cr in FY22 to ₹13,980 cr in FY26 (13% a year), led by India (₹4,286 cr → ₹7,645 cr) and Brazil, while the US and Germany barely grew. FY26 was +21%, of which the base business +15% and JB (consolidated for 70 days from 21-Jan-2026) the rest. EBITDA margin rose every year, from 28.6% to 32.6%, as India's branded, chronic-heavy mix grew and generics shrank in the mix. Reported profit to shareholders rose from ₹777 cr (FY22, after a ₹299 cr impairment) to ₹2,163 cr (FY26), EPS ₹22.97 → ₹63.92. **The deal changes the base:** with JB for a full year, its brand amortisation (₹1,340 cr a year) and interest on ₹12,500 cr of acquisition debt, pro forma FY26 profit is only ₹1,333 cr, or ₹35.0 a share on the 38.04 cr shares that trade today. That is the base our forecasts grow from.

blocks.p: Torrent grows in India by buying brands and pushing them through a bigger, better-paid field force: Elder's India business (FY15, ₹1,960 cr outflow), Unichem's India business (FY18, ~₹3,940 cr), Curatio (Oct-2022, ₹2,000 cr) and now JB (₹12,537 cr in cash for 48.8% plus 4.19 cr new shares, ~₹20,100 cr at ₹4,800, for the rest). Each deal was debt-funded and each cut returns before lifting them: ROCE fell from 48% (FY16) to 13% (FY18-19) after Unichem and recovered to 27% by FY25; it fell to 15% in FY26 with JB. Capex is modest (₹430-680 cr a year, 4-5% of revenue) and the company pays out 55-60% of profit as dividends.

sections.title: Earnings quality: good cash conversion, but read four things carefully after the deal

bullets: **Acquisition amortisation.** JB's brands (₹19,627 cr), customer relationships (₹940 cr) and licences (₹124 cr) are amortised over up to 15 years: ~₹1,340 cr a year, ₹257 cr in the 70 days of FY26 and ~₹335 cr in Q1FY27. It is not tax-deductible; a deferred-tax credit of ~₹337 cr a year offsets part of it, so it costs ~₹1,000 cr a year of reported profit (~₹26 a share) but no cash. Torrent's older brand amortisation (~₹543 cr a year in FY24-25) was already in its history.

**Three EPS bases.** FY26 reported EPS ₹63.92 is on 33.84 cr shares with a 51.2% minority in JB; Q1FY27 EPS ₹14.87 is on the post-merger count (Screener shows ₹16.72); our FY26 pro forma (₹35.0) has JB for a full year with a full year of amortisation and deal interest. Growth rates across these bases mean little.

**Hedging losses in other income.** Forward contracts lost ₹183 cr in FY26 as the rupee fell (₹45 cr in Q3FY26 alone), while revenue gained from the same move; other income was −₹94 cr. Earlier years: +₹170 cr (FY22), −₹18 cr, −₹4 cr, −₹17 cr.

**Exceptional items and EBITDA definitions.** FY26 exceptional costs of ₹89 cr (₹70 cr deal costs, ₹19 cr JB distributor severance) and ₹21 cr in Q1FY27 (integration). The Q4FY26 press-release EBITDA excluded JB ESOP charges (CFO). PLI income of ₹147 cr is in revenue.

**Cash conversion.** Operating cash flow was 69% of EBITDA in FY25 and 66% of reported EBITDA in FY26 (inventory and receivables built up; JB working capital came in); FY24 was 97%. Inventory days are high (~330) because Torrent supplies many export markets.
**Audit.** B S R & Co. (KPMG network), unmodified; the JB purchase-price allocation was done by an independent valuer.

blocks.callout: **Accounting flag: AMBER.** Nothing aggressive, but the deal makes the numbers hard to read: non-cash amortisation that will last ~15 years, a pro forma base, hedging losses in other income and EBITDA "before ESOP". We show reported and amortisation-adjusted EPS side by side; our primary method (EV/EBITDA) is unaffected by the charge, and our P/E cross-check uses the adjusted figure because the P/E history never carried it.

sections.title: Net debt from ₹2,500 cr to ₹12,900 cr; on our numbers it falls below 1x EBITDA by FY29

blocks.p: Torrent funded JB with debt: borrowings rose from ₹3,026 cr (Mar-25) to ₹14,798 cr (Mar-26): ₹11,161 cr of NCDs (₹10,990 cr raised in Jan-2026 at 7.45-7.80% plus ₹400 cr of older bonds), ₹1,420 cr of commercial paper, ₹1,495 cr of working-capital loans and ₹723 cr of term loans, plus ₹227 cr of leases. Against this it holds ₹2,031 cr of cash, deposits and liquid funds (₹1,155 cr came with JB). Net debt was ₹12,684 cr excluding leases, 2.3x combined EBITDA (company); 2.07x in Q1FY27. Management's target at the deal was below 0.5x within 2-3 years. Our own net-debt path, which adds back the ~₹337 cr a year of tax the engine does not see (JB's brand amortisation is not tax-deductible), gives 1.6x, 1.1x, 0.6x at Mar-27/28/29: slower than the target because we assume dividends continue at half of profit.

**Biggest swing factors:** JB's margin and India growth. Each 1pp of group EBITDA margin is ~₹217 cr of FY28E EBITDA, worth ~₹126 a share at 21x Sep-28E EBITDA; each 1x on the multiple is ~₹210 a share.

head: Term
What it means
rows: Off-patent medicines sold under the company's own brand name and promoted to doctors (India, Brazil). Prices and loyalty are higher than for plain generics.
Unbranded copies sold on price to wholesalers, pharmacy chains or insurers (German tenders); prices fall every year.
Indian pharmaceutical market (retail prescription sales tracked by AIOCD Pharmatrac / IQVIA).
Medicines taken for years (cardiac, diabetes, CNS), for weeks to months (gastro, pain, VMN), or for days (antibiotics). Chronic sales are steadier.
Medical representatives who visit doctors; PCPM = sales per rep per month (Torrent ~₹10 lakh).
A brand family including all its strengths and combinations; Torrent has 27 above ₹100 cr a year.
Contract development and manufacturing for other pharma companies (JB makes lozenges for multinationals).
NCLT, scheme of amalgamation, appointed date

The National Company Law Tribunal approves mergers; the appointed date (21-Jan-2026) is when the merger takes effect in the accounts; the effective date (8-Jul-2026) is when it became legally complete.
Shares of the acquirer given per share of the target: 51 Torrent shares for every 100 JB shares.
The part of a subsidiary owned by outsiders (51.2% of JB from Jan to Jul-2026); eliminated when the merger shares were issued.

On an acquisition, the price is allocated to the target's assets at fair value, including brands (₹19,627 cr for JB), which are then expensed over their useful life (up to 15 years): ~₹1,340 cr a year, non-cash.
Tax the accounts set aside because the book value of the brands exceeds their tax value; it unwinds as the brands are amortised, lowering book tax (~₹337 cr a year).
Reported EPS plus the JB brand amortisation net of its deferred-tax credit, per share: the basis on which we compare the forward P/E with Torrent's pre-deal history.
FY26 restated as if JB had been owned 100% from 1-Apr-2025, with a full year of brand amortisation and acquisition interest, on 38.04 cr shares.
Non-convertible debentures (bonds) and commercial paper (short-term debt) used to fund the deal.
Borrowings (incl. leases) less cash and liquid investments, divided by a year's EBITDA: a leverage measure.
Growth in local currency, removing the effect of exchange-rate moves on rupee revenue.
Brazil's and the US drug regulators; an ANDA is a US generic-drug approval.
Enterprise value (market value plus net debt) ÷ EBITDA; share price ÷ earnings per share.
Half of FY28E plus half of FY29E: the 12-month-forward earnings the market will look at in September 2027.
Discounted cash flow valuation; WACC is the required return on all capital (here 11.2%).

assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Torrent Pharmaceuticals (consolidated, ₹ crore), on the basis that holds over the target horizon: Torrent with 100% of J.B. Chemicals & Pharmaceuticals (JB) merged in (scheme effective 8-Jul-2026, appointed date 21-Jan-2026) and 38.04 cr shares (4.19 cr allotted on 20-Jul-2026). The base year FY26 is a pro forma combined year (TORNTPHARM.patch.js: revenue ₹17,352 cr per AR FY26 note 42; acquisition interest for the full year), so FY27E growth is like-for-like. One reportable segment (generic formulations), so the engine runs on a single revenue-growth path; the business-line build (India base, JB India, Brazil, US, Germany, rest of world, JB international & CDMO) sits in `businessLines` and the authoring script checks it sums to model revenue. Depreciation includes ₹1,340 cr a year of amortisation of JB's brands and customer relationships created in the purchase accounting (not tax-deductible; a deferred-tax credit offsets it in book tax). No minorities from FY27. Valued on EV/EBITDA on Sep-28E EBITDA, as Prabhudas Lilladher and ICICI Direct do (unaffected by the JB amortisation and the new debt); P/E on EPS before the JB amortisation (Motilal Oswal's method) and a DCF are cross-checks.
assumptions._revenueWhy: Sum of the business-line build below, on the pro forma FY26 base of ₹17,352 cr (reported FY26 ₹13,980 cr had JB for 70 days). FY27E ₹19,513 cr = +40% on reported FY26, +12.5% like-for-like: India base +16% (Q1 +19%, management 'mid-teens', semaglutide injectable out of stock Jul-Aug), JB India +10% (Q1 +13%; brand transfers to Torrent divisions disrupt Q2-Q3; management 'double-digit still possible'), Brazil +16% in rupees (Q1 +3% in BRL after a one-off channel destocking; mid-teens from Q2), US +12% in rupees (Q1 +23% in dollars incl. one-offs; single-digit dollar growth guided), Germany +4% (supplier out of business, lost tenders), rest of world +8%, JB international and CDMO +10% ('high single to low double digit'). FY28-29E: India base +14%/+13%, JB India +11% (revenue synergies only from FY28), Brazil +13%/+12%, US +6%/+5%, Germany +4%, rest of world +8%, JB international +10%.

businessLines._why: FY26 pro forma by line: Torrent's FY26 split (AR FY26 MD&A: India ₹7,645 cr, US ₹1,363 cr, Germany ₹1,249 cr, Brazil ₹1,362 cr, others ₹2,361 cr) less JB's 70-day contribution (₹775 cr: India ₹438 cr = Q4 India ₹2,215 cr less Torrent base India ₹1,777 cr [Q4FY25 ₹1,545 cr +15%], international ₹337 cr), plus JB's full FY26 revenue (₹4,148 cr, Screener JBCHEPHARM) split 61/39 India/international as in Q1FY27 (₹733 cr / ₹468 cr of ₹1,201 cr). Growth rates are explained in _revenueWhy.

assumptions._marginWhy: Q1FY27 33.8% (Torrent base 33.3%, JB 35.3% vs 28.8% a year earlier). Built from the two businesses: Torrent base margin +50bp a year (management's standing guidance: 32.8% FY26 → 33.3% / 33.8% / 34.3%); JB 35.5% / 37.5% / 38.5% as the ₹400-450 cr cost synergies (guided for year 3, 'tracking ahead', FY27 'definitely above ₹100 cr') are delivered, against 26.7% in JB's own FY26 books. Weighted: 33.8% / 34.7% / 35.3%. Each 1pp of margin is ~₹217 cr of FY28E EBITDA (~₹4.2 of EPS).
assumptions._capexWhy: FY26 ₹677 cr (incl. JB for 70 days), FY25 ₹612 cr; JB's own capex ~₹110-200 cr a year (cash flow FY24-26). Combined ~₹800 cr in FY27E rising with revenue (~4% of sales). No acquisitions assumed: management will wait 12-18 months before the next deal.
assumptions._depWhy: Q1FY27 D&A ₹593 cr (₹2,372 cr annualised): Torrent ~₹205 cr a quarter, JB's own ~₹45 cr, ~₹335 cr of amortisation of JB brands and customer relationships (₹1,340 cr a year: the Q4FY26 stub was ₹257 cr for 70 days and the CFO said to use it for the full year; brands ₹19,627 cr amortised over up to 15 years). 5.83% of the average gross block (₹40,426 cr at Mar-26 incl. ₹20,691 cr of JB intangibles) gives ₹2,380 / 2,428 / 2,479 cr. CWIP is held flat by the engine.
assumptions._treasuryWhy: Set to zero because the engine applies the yield to net cash, which is negative (net debt ₹12,684 cr at Mar-26). Treasury income on the gross cash and fund balance is built in otherIncome instead.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Built from sourced parts (AR FY26 note 29). (1) Treasury income: interest ₹38.4 cr + mutual-fund gains ₹30.9 cr = ₹69.4 cr in FY26, when JB's ₹1,155 cr of cash and funds came in only in January; gross cash, bank and funds ₹2,031 cr at Mar-26, assumed ₹1,500 cr from Mar-27 as surplus cash repays commercial paper; 6.25% gives ₹110 cr in FY27E and ₹94 cr a year after. (2) Foreign exchange and hedging: +₹170 cr FY22, -₹18 cr FY23, -₹4 cr FY24, -₹17 cr FY25, -₹183 cr FY26 (forward-cover losses as the rupee fell; ~₹45 cr in Q3FY26 alone), still negative in Q1FY27 (PL: other income -₹12 cr 'led by forex loss'): we take -₹100 cr in FY27E, -₹40 cr in FY28E and -₹20 cr in FY29E as the old hedges run off (FY23-25 average -₹13 cr). (3) Recurring miscellaneous non-operating income ₹3 cr (FY26 ₹2.8 cr). Left out as one-offs: asset-sale gains (₹17.7 cr in FY26) and exceptional items (FY26 -₹89 cr: ₹70 cr deal costs and ₹19 cr JB distribution severance; Q1FY27 -₹21 cr). Total ₹13 / 57 / 77 cr vs FY26 -₹94 cr (reported other income) and -₹69 cr in the twelve months to Jun-26 (Screener, before exceptional items).
assumptions._interestLabel: Interest on borrowings (₹10,990 cr acquisition NCDs at 7.45-7.80%) and leases
assumptions._interestWhy: Q1FY27 finance cost ₹305 cr on ₹14,798 cr of borrowings (Mar-26: NCDs ₹11,161 cr, commercial paper ₹1,420 cr, working-capital loans ₹1,495 cr, term loans ₹723 cr) plus ₹227 cr of leases. Acquisition debt raised in Jan-2026: ₹1,500 cr one-year CP and NCDs of ₹2,000 / 2,500 / 3,000 / 3,500 cr maturing in 2, 3, 4 and 5 years at 7.45% / 7.60% / 7.70% / 7.80% (weighted 7.66%). Built as 7.7% on average gross borrowings (our net-debt path in the authoring script plus ₹1,500-2,031 cr of gross cash) plus ~₹55 cr of lease and other finance costs: borrowings fall from ₹14,798 cr to ~₹12,700 / 9,900 / 6,700 cr at Mar-27/28/29 as free cash flow repays CP and working-capital lines, then the ₹2,100 cr and ₹2,590 cr NCD maturities (FY28, FY29).
assumptions._taxWhy: Book tax on profit after the JB brand amortisation: FY26 25.6% (₹734 cr on ₹2,872 cr), Q1FY27 22.8% (current tax ₹254 cr, deferred-tax credit ₹87 cr on ₹733 cr). The brand amortisation is not tax-deductible, but the deferred tax liability created in the purchase accounting unwinds at 25.17% of it, so the book rate stays near the statutory 25.17%. No minorities after the merger (JB's subsidiaries are wholly owned).
assumptions._payoutWhy: Torrent paid out 57-59% of profit in FY24-26 (FY26: ₹29 interim + ₹9 final = ₹38 a share on 33.84 cr shares). We assume 50% while net debt is above ~1x EBITDA (management targets deleveraging over 2-3 years); DPS ~₹31 / ₹41 / ₹52.

dcf._betaWhy: The engine discounts at the cost of equity; beta 0.78 gives 11.2%, equal to our WACC: market value ~₹1.83 lakh cr, net debt ₹12,684 cr (6.5% of capital) at 7.7% pre-tax (5.8% after tax), cost of equity ~11.6% at beta 0.85 for a defensive, domestically led pharma company.
dcf._tgWhy: 6% nominal: India branded generics (~55% of revenue) grow 8-10% a year in value; Germany and the US grow little.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from ~11% to 8% by year 15 as the India franchise matures and export markets stay low-growth.
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: 35%: a little below the FY29E 35.3% (base margin +50bp a year cannot continue forever; price controls, trade generics).
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: 4.5% of revenue: maintenance plus capacity for 8% growth (FY24-27E 3.5-4.8%).
dcf._depWhy: 5% of revenue = tax-deductible depreciation and amortisation only (book D&A ex-JB brand amortisation ~5.3% of FY27E revenue). The JB brand amortisation is excluded because it gives no tax saving; including it would overstate cash flow.

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: India keeps growing mid-teens (semaglutide recovers, Curatio +30%), the JB brand transfer is smooth and revenue synergies start in FY28, Brazil approves generic semaglutide, and cost synergies reach ₹450 cr a year early.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: The JB integration loses prescribers (as some past brand transfers did), India growth slips back to ~10% as the market normalises, Germany keeps losing tenders, semaglutide prices collapse, and synergies are reinvested rather than banked.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.why: How the street values Torrent: two of the three post-Q1 notes that disclose a method use EV/EBITDA on FY28E (Prabhudas Lilladher 28x, ICICI Direct 27x; Motilal Oswal uses P/E). EV/EBITDA is also unaffected by the two things the JB deal changed: ~₹1,340 cr a year of non-cash brand amortisation and the new debt. 21x = Torrent's 19.9x median one-year-forward EV/EBITDA since Apr-2021 (computed in our files: before the deal on Torrent's own 33.84 cr shares, net debt and standalone EBITDA; after the 29-Jun-2025 announcement on 38.04 cr shares, the deal debt and combined forward EBITDA; no trough years) x 1.0555 (pharma peers' median trailing EV/EBITDA vs five-year medians at 30-Sep-2026, excluding Torrent: the EV/EBITDA analogue of the PLAYBOOK §7c P/E factor, as for hospitals) = 21.0x. Bull 26x and bear 18x = the 75th (24.8x) and 25th (17.1x) percentiles x 1.0555. Sep-28E EBITDA less net debt at Sep-28E (model).

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: Cross-check on earnings (Motilal Oswal's method). 42x Sep-28E EPS BEFORE the JB brand amortisation (₹1,340 cr a year, ~₹26 a share after its deferred-tax credit), because the P/E history is pre-deal Torrent that never carried it: Torrent's 40.0x median one-year-forward P/E since Apr-2021 on EPS before exceptional items (batch rule, as Sun Pharma and Cipla) x 1.0545 (PLAYBOOK §7c pharma P/E factor) = 42.2x → 42x. The engine values reported EPS, so the multiple here is the equivalent on reported Sep-28E EPS (42 x adjusted ÷ reported: base 53.66x; bull 46.5x and bear 36x on the adjusted basis, translated the same way). Checked in TORNTPHARM.ctx.js.

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: Tests whether cash flows support the price: 15-year FCFF at 11.2% (beta set so the cost of equity equals our WACC), terminal growth 6%; tax shield only on tax-deductible depreciation (JB brand amortisation excluded); less net debt at Mar-27.

otherTreasury.label: Offset: minority interest (₹9,196 cr, now equity) and deferred tax on JB brands (₹5,670 cr) in other liabilities
otherTreasury._why: Engine workaround (TORNTPHARM.patch.js note 2). Screener's Mar-26 other liabilities, which the Excel model reads unpatched, include the ₹9,196.40 cr non-controlling interest (now owners' equity after the merger) and the ₹5,670.04 cr deferred tax liability; neither is working capital. This negative entry takes both out of working capital (13.45% of pro forma revenue) in the engine and the Excel alike; investments are raised by the same amount in the patch, so net debt is unchanged at ₹12,913 cr incl. leases, and CWIP is lowered by the DTL so the balance sheet balances.

EV/EBITDA is also unaffected by the two things the JB deal changed: ~₹1,340 cr a year of non-cash brand amortisation and the new debt. 21x = Torrent's 19.9x median one-year-forward EV/EBITDA since Apr-2021 (computed in our files: before the deal on Torrent's own 33.84 cr shares, net debt and standalone EBITDA; after the 29-Jun-2025 announcement on 38.04 cr shares, the deal debt and combined forward EBITDA; no trough years) x 1.0555 (pharma peers' median trailing EV/EBITDA vs five-year medians at 30-Sep-2026, excluding Torrent: the EV/EBITDA analogue of the PLAYBOOK §7c P/E factor, as for hospitals) = 21.0x. Bull 26x and bear 18x = the 75th (24.8x) and 25th (17.1x) percentiles x 1.0555. Sep-28E EBITDA less net debt at Sep-28E (model).

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: The JB integration loses prescribers (as some past brand transfers did), India growth slips back to ~10% as the market normalises, Germany keeps losing tenders, semaglutide prices collapse, and synergies are reinvested rather than banked.

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: Cross-check on earnings (Motilal Oswal's method). 42x Sep-28E EPS BEFORE the JB brand amortisation (₹1,340 cr a year, ~₹26 a share after its deferred-tax credit), because the P/E history is pre-deal Torrent that never carried it: Torrent's 40.0x median one-year-forward P/E since Apr-2021 on EPS before exceptional items (batch rule, as Sun Pharma and Cipla) x 1.0545 (PLAYBOOK §7c pharma P/E factor) = 42.2x → 42x. The engine values reported EPS, so the multiple here is the equivalent on reported Sep-28E EPS (42 x adjusted ÷ reported: base 53.66x; bull 46.5x and bear 36x on the adjusted basis, translated the same way). Checked in TORNTPHARM.ctx.js.

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: Tests whether cash flows support the price: 15-year FCFF at 11.2% (beta set so the cost of equity equals our WACC), terminal growth 6%; tax shield only on tax-deductible depreciation (JB brand amortisation excluded); less net debt at Mar-27.
